title: DataSentinel: A Game-Theoretic Detection of Prompt Injection Attacks
abstract: DataSentinel is a game-theoretic method to detect prompt injection attacks in LLM-integrated applications. It fine-tunes a detection LLM to detect inputs contaminated with injected prompts that are strategically adapted to evade detection.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content:
Imagine you're trying to have a conversation with a language model, but someone keeps interrupting with misleading information. That's similar to what happens in prompt injection attacks. DataSentinel is designed to detect these interruptions and prevent them from misleading the language model.

The key idea is to fine-tune a detection language model to be more vulnerable to prompt injection attacks, which may seem counterintuitive. However, this increased vulnerability is turned into a defense mechanism, making it more effective at detecting contaminated target data.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content:
DataSentinel formulates the fine-tuning of the detection LLM as a minimax optimization problem, which simulates a game between the detector and the attacker. The goal is to fine-tune the detection LLM to accurately distinguish between contaminated and clean target data.

The detection LLM is fine-tuned using a dataset of contaminated and clean target data, and the fine-tuning process involves alternating between the inner max problem and the outer min problem.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content:
DataSentinel is evaluated on 7 target tasks, each corresponding to a dataset, 9 injected tasks, 6 LLMs, and 9 existing prompt injection attacks. The results show that DataSentinel is consistently highly effective at detecting contaminated target data, achieving a false positive rate (FPR) close to 0 and a false negative rate (FNR) close to 0 for several prompt injection attacks.

For instance, DataSentinel achieves a FPR of 0.0 and a FNR of 0.0 for the 'Ignore previous instructions' attack, and a FPR of 0.0 and a FNR of 0.07 for the 'Optimization-based' attack.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content:
DataSentinel has significant implications for the security of LLM-integrated applications. By effectively detecting prompt injection attacks, DataSentinel can prevent attackers from misleading language models and compromising the confidentiality and intellectual property of application developers.

Moreover, DataSentinel's game-theoretic approach provides a new perspective on the cat-and-mouse game between attackers and defenders, highlighting the importance of considering strong adaptive attacks in the design of detection methods.

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content:
DataSentinel's key innovations include its game-theoretic approach to detecting prompt injection attacks and its fine-tuning of the detection LLM to be more vulnerable to attacks.

By turning the detection LLM's increased vulnerability into a defense mechanism, DataSentinel provides a new and effective way to detect contaminated target data.

sections.title: Try It Yourself
sections.content:
To try DataSentinel yourself, you can access the code and data at https://github.com/liu00222/Open-Prompt-Injection.

You can also experiment with different detection instructions and secret keys to see how DataSentinel performs in different scenarios.
